title: Add Histogram Chart Mark

complexity.rationale: The rect-mark rendering reuses Bar's existing mark construction directly. The only non-precedented piece is the data layer: binning a single continuous `value` field via Vega's built-in `bin` transform plus a `count` aggregate — a standard, fully-documented Vega transform with a known API (extent/explicit range + maxbins), not a bespoke algorithm to design. Supporting an explicit bin count/range override is the same `bin` transform with different input parameters, not new logic.

summary: A single-series bar-like mark over a continuous `value` field, binned into equal-width buckets via Vega's `bin` transform and rendered with Bar's existing rect-mark construction. No color/series channel, no legend.
requirements: Accepts a single required `value` (continuous/quantitative) channel — no dimension, color, or series channel
Auto-bins `value` into equal-width buckets using Vega's `bin` transform by default, then aggregates a `count` per bucket
Also supports an explicit bin count and/or explicit min/max range override, passed through to the same `bin` transform's `maxbins`/`extent` parameters instead of the auto-computed values
Renders one rect per bucket using Bar's existing rect-mark construction (single static color, no grouping/stacking)
No legend — Histogram never has a color/series facet to key one off of
X-axis domain reflects bin boundaries, not discrete category labels

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Render the existing EmptyState, matching Bar's current empty-data behavior.
Render a single bin containing that one value; bin transform must not divide-by-zero when extent min equals max.
Degenerate extent (min === max) — bin transform must fall back to a single bucket rather than producing NaN bin boundaries.

edgeCases.case: Non-numeric or null values in the value field
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Excluded from binning, consistent with how other continuous-scale marks in this codebase already drop null/non-numeric values before scale domain calculation.

edgeCases.case: An explicit min/max range narrower than the data's actual extent
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Values outside the explicit range are excluded from binning (clipped), not clamped into the edge buckets, rather than silently expanding the range back to the data extent.

Bin count/width does not change with container width in this initial version — only bar width shrinks, matching Bar's existing responsive behavior; document this as an intentional v1 limitation rather than dynamic re-binning.
Rect fill resolves through the same static-color-value pattern Bar already uses for single-series bars.
S1-only for this spec; no S2 port until the mark stabilizes out of rc status.
SVG root aria-label should describe the value range/bin count, not per-category labels, since bins aren't discrete categories.

crossCutting.notes: touchesHoverAnimation: reuses Bar's existing hover-animation gate on rect marks. touchesTooltipOrPopover: reuses Bar's existing ChartTooltip/ChartPopover wiring so hovering a bucket can show its count — no new interactive-mark plumbing needed, just applied to a bucketed data source instead of a categorical one. requiresNewSignalOrScale: false — the x scale is a plain continuous/linear scale over bin boundaries, using the same scale-building helpers Bar/Scatter already share; no new scale type. requiresS1S2Parity: false because this ships as a new s1-only rc-status mark, matching the Donut/BigNumber precedent; revisit once promoted out of rc.

implementationPlan.change: Create HistogramOptions/HistogramOptionsWithDefaults/HistogramSpecOptions with a required `value` field, an optional `maxBins` option (default provided, auto-binning), and optional `binMin`/`binMax` overrides passed to the bin transform's `extent`.
Add HistogramOptions to the MarkOptions union.

New addBinTransform helper building a Vega `bin` transform (extent + maxbins, with extent overridable via binMin/binMax) on `value` followed by an `aggregate` transform producing `count` per bin — no existing bar util to reuse here, this is new data-layer logic.
getHistogramMark, reusing barUtils.ts's/barSpecBuilder.ts's rect-mark construction pattern (getBarMark-equivalent) but keyed off bin0/bin1 fields instead of a categorical dimension.

addHistogram, addData (calls the new bin/aggregate helper), addSignals (reuse bar's interactive-mark signal helpers), setScales (linear scale over bin boundaries + linear count scale), modeled on barSpecBuilder.ts's addBar with dimension/color/stacking options removed.
Unit tests for getHistogramMark using the new fixture.
Per-function tests for addData (asserting the bin/aggregate transform shape), addSignals, setScales.
Register histogramCount: -1 in initializeComponentCounts, import addHistogram, add the 'histogram' switch case.
HistogramProps/HistogramElement, Omit-ing only fields replaced at the React boundary (ChartTooltip/ChartPopover children).
Render-null component holding prop defaults, placed under rc/ per the Donut/BigNumber rc-status precedent.
Import Histogram from '../rc' and add its displayName dispatch case.
Add Histogram to the sanitizeRscChartChildren import/list from '../rc'.
Update the toStrictEqual ChartOptions snapshot to include the new mark type at default values.
Basic story with a raw continuous-value dataset.

openQuestions: What is the default maxBins value when no explicit binMin/binMax/maxBins is given (auto-binning path)?
Should Histogram support a pre-binned data shape (caller supplies bin0/bin1/count directly) as an alternative to raw-value auto-binning, similar to Box Plot's raw-vs-precomputed dual mode?
